problems.formal_statement:
theorem EulerMascheroni.Sondow.integral_identity (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    I n = ((2*n).choose n : ℝ) * Real.eulerMascheroniConstant + L n - (A n : ℝ) := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
For every positive integer $n$,
$$I_n=\binom{2n}{n}\gamma+L_n-A_n.$$
This is a known analytic identity, left as a formalization obligation.
problems.source: Jonathan Sondow, Criteria for Irrationality of Euler's Constant, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209070 (v2, 4 October 2002). Theorem 1, equation (7), pp. 6-9.

problems.formal_statement:
theorem EulerMascheroni.Sondow.scaled_integral_bounds (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    0 < (d (2*n) : ℝ) * I n ∧ (d (2*n) : ℝ) * I n < (1/2 : ℝ)^n := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
For every positive integer $n$,
$$0<d_{2n}I_n<2^{-n}.$$
This follows from the established bounds $d_{2n}<8^n$ and $0<I_n<16^{-n}$. It is a known estimate awaiting formalization.
problems.source: Jonathan Sondow, Criteria for Irrationality of Euler's Constant, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209070 (v2, 4 October 2002). Lemma 3, p. 10.

problems.theorem_title: Clearing the denominators of Sondow harmonic sums
problems.formal_statement:
theorem EulerMascheroni.Sondow.scaled_A_integral (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ z : ℤ, (d (2*n) : ℝ) * (A n : ℝ) = z := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
For every nonnegative integer $n$,
$$d_{2n}A_n\in\mathbb Z.$$
The endpoint $n=0$ gives zero. This arithmetic fact clears the harmonic denominators in the integral identity.
problems.source: Jonathan Sondow, Criteria for Irrationality of Euler's Constant, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209070 (v2, 4 October 2002). Theorem 1, p. 6; denominator observation following equation (11), p. 8.

problems.theorem_title: Open Sondow fractional-part condition for Euler irrationality
problems.formal_statement:
theorem EulerMascheroni.Sondow.fractional_lower_bound_conjecture :
    ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ n ∧ 0 < n ∧
      (1/2 : ℝ)^n ≤ Int.fract ((d (2*n) : ℝ) * L n) := by sorry
problems.natural_language_statement:
Conjectural arithmetic condition: for every natural number $N$, there is an integer $n\ge\max(N,1)$ such that
$$\{d_{2n}L_n\}\ge2^{-n}.$$
Here $\{x\}=x-\lfloor x\rfloor$. This is the sufficient hypothesis of Sondow's Corollary 6, not a theorem proved in that paper. It is the unresolved arithmetic ingredient of this proposed route to irrationality; finite numerical evidence does not establish it.
problems.source: Jonathan Sondow, Criteria for Irrationality of Euler's Constant, https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0209070 (v2, 4 October 2002). Corollary 6, p. 11; numerical discussion p. 4. Only the conditional implication is established by the source; the displayed infinite-occurrence assertion is an open conjectural target.
